public_rationale: FutureSearch modeled positive API margins for June 2024 and an August-pricing scenario, but its August 7, 2026 review says those estimates remain unchecked [e1]. The model supplies neither verified August 2024 losses on every use and every power user nor a verified profitable counterexample [e1]. The firm assertions about every use and every power user therefore remain unresolved [e1].
limitations: The packet lacks verified August 2024 revenue and serving costs matched to individual uses or subscriber accounts.
The API model does not establish profitability across all products, premium subscribers, or power users.
Company-wide losses cannot establish losses on every use or every power user.
Subscription-revenue allocation and a numerical definition of power users remain unspecified.
The premium-subscriber clause expresses doubt and is not assessed as a firm assertion of universal losses.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI loses money on every use of its product, probably makes no profit on premium subscribers, and loses money on power users.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI loses money every single time that somebody uses their product, and while it might make money selling premium subscriptions, I severely doubt it’s turning a profit on these customers, and certainly losing money on any and all power users.

our_interpretation: The firm assertions concern losses on every use and every power user. The premium-subscriber clause expresses doubt and is not treated as a firm universal prediction.
The ordinary reading compares revenue attributable to usage or a subscriber with the costs of serving that usage or subscriber. Company-wide losses alone do not establish this.
For the ongoing state, I use August 2024, the latest completed monthly reporting period identified in the supplied context before publication.
I interpret power users as unusually heavy users, but do not invent a numerical usage threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable service-level and subscriber-level data for the target period establish negative contribution on every relevant use and every heavy-user account, with revenue and service costs allocated consistently.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable matching-period data identify a profitable use or heavy-user account, or a positive aggregate contribution that necessarily includes profitable uses under the same revenue and cost definitions.

evidence.locator: How This Held Up, paragraph beginning 'The margin numbers'
evidence.explanation: The authors modeled positive API margins for June 2024 and under August pricing, which challenges the inference that overall losses imply losses on every use. Their retrospective explicitly says those estimates remain unverified; neither the period nor the customer scope establishes the claimed universal outcome.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verified August 2024 revenue and serving costs, allocated consistently across uses and accounts, with a defined heavy-user cohort. Evidence establishing negative contribution on every relevant use and every heavy-user account would support the firm assertions. A profitable use or heavy-user account, or positive aggregate contribution that necessarily includes profitable uses, would contradict the corresponding universal assertion.
